cards.text: Friend, we're in Judah, where Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat just succeeded his father as king. Up in Israel, the king is Joram son of Ahab, in his fifth year. Joram and Jehoram, two kings, SAME TIME, and somebody's mail is going to the wrong palace EVERY week.
Jehoram is thirty-two when he becomes king, and he reigns in Jerusalem eight years. Eight YEARS on a throne, and I can't keep a batch of dough in the fridge eight DAYS before somebody eats it.
Now here's a detail that matters. Jehoram marries a daughter of Ahab, so Joram's own family is right there in his house.

cards.question: With a daughter of Ahab as his wife, whose ways does Jehoram walk in?

answers.text: The ways of the kings of Israel
The ways of his father Jehoshaphat
The ways of the prophet Elisha

cards.question: Jehoram does evil in the sight of the LORD.
With an evil king on Judah's throne, the LORD is ready to destroy Judah.
The LORD is unwilling to destroy Judah for the sake of His servant ___.

cards.text: The LORD had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark drawer, so trust me, nobody gets excited about one little light like I do.
In Jehoram's days, Edom rebels against the hand of Judah. They are DONE taking orders.

cards.question: Edom doesn't stop at rebelling against Judah. They appoint their own ___.

cards.text: So Jehoram crosses over to Zair with ALL his chariots, and the Edomites surround him and his chariot commanders anyway. Every chariot he owns, and he's STILL boxed in.

cards.question: Jehoram is surrounded by the Edomites at Zair. What does he do?

answers.text: He rises up and attacks by night
He hands his chariots over to Edom
He sends a messenger to ask for peace

cards.question: After the night attack at Zair, Jehoram's troops stand firm beside him.

cards.text: Nope, his troops flee to their homes. It's like calling a big team meeting at work, turning around, and EVERYBODY already clocked out.

cards.question: After Zair, where does Edom stand with Judah?

answers.text: Still in rebellion to this day
Back under the hand of Judah

cards.text: Edom's not alone either: Libnah rebels at the same time, and Jehoram's kingdom is starting to look like a group chat where everybody keeps hitting leave. The rest of what Jehoram did is written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Next stretch, friend, and Judah's about to get a new king. Jehoram rests with his fathers and is buried with them.

cards.question: Jehoram is buried with his fathers. Where is that?

cards.text: His son Ahaziah reigns in his place. That's the twelfth year of Joram over Israel.
Ahaziah is twenty-two, and he reigns in Jerusalem one year. His mother is Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel, so this new king's family tree runs right up north.

cards.question: Ahaziah turns things around and does right in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Nope, Ahaziah walks in the ways of the house of Ahab and does evil like them, and the text says why: "for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab." Some families pass down a great cookie recipe, and this one keeps passing down the burnt batch.

cards.question: Ahaziah heads to Ramoth-gilead for a fight. Who goes with him?
At Ramoth-gilead, Ahaziah and Joram fight against ___ king of Aram.
In the fight at Ramoth-gilead, the Arameans wound Ahaziah king of Judah.

cards.text: So King Joram goes back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans gave him at Ramah, when he fought Hazael. A king, laid up and healing.

cards.question: Joram is laid up in Jezreel with his wounds, so Ahaziah goes down there to ___ him.

cards.text: Ahaziah goes down to Jezreel to visit Joram, because Joram had been wounded. Say what you want about Ahaziah, but he shows up, which is more than Jehoram's troops did at Zair.

findings.problem: The question reverses who goes with whom. It says Ahaziah heads to Ramoth-gilead and asks who goes with him, but 2 Kings 8:28 says Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab. The text makes Ahaziah the one joining Joram.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card's first sentence repeats what card 11 just asked and answered: Ahaziah goes down to Jezreel to visit Joram because Joram was wounded. The rest of the card is only a joke, so the card is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.

Most story cards in stop 2 are flat and lack Papa Dorin's voice. Card 1, card 3 ("That's the twelfth year of Joram over Israel."), card 4 and card 10 ("A king, laid up and healing.") read as plain summary or filler. The only real jokes are on cards 6 and 12, which is a sharp drop from stop 1.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
